draft.title: Why some texts endure
card: Some texts are still studied generations after they were written. Readers keep returning to them for reasons.
Many explore lasting human questions, such as love, power, loss or identity, which matter in every era.
Many use language with unusual skill, so that word choices and structure give pleasure and meaning.
Many reward rereading, since a second visit reveals new layers. You can argue what makes a text worth studying, using evidence.
draft.remember: Enduring texts ask lasting questions, use language skilfully and reward rereading.

a.q: Which feature most helps a text to endure across generations?
opts: It explores questions that matter in any era
It was published a very long time ago
It is easy to read in one sitting
It is set in the reader's own town
a.why: Texts endure when they explore lasting human questions that readers in any era care about. Age alone does not make a text last, because many old texts are forgotten.
a.clue: Think about what stays true for every generation.

b.q: A class debates why an old play is still performed. Which argument best explains its lasting appeal?
opts: Its themes of jealousy and ambition still feel familiar
It is famous, so schools must keep teaching it
It has a plot that is simple to follow
It uses words no modern reader can understand
b.why: A lasting human question, such as jealousy or ambition, links the play to readers today. Fame alone is not a reason in the text. Difficult words do not explain appeal.
b.clue: Look for a reason about ideas, not reputation.

a.best: It explores questions that matter in any era

b.best: Its themes of jealousy and ambition still feel familiar
